reviewedRevision: 22fe11aa (accepted build) plus the fixes in this commit
reviewer: mimic-fair, mimic-robust and mimic-present (parallel split review)
process: Lean final review at the user's request, with the review split across three parallel reviewers (fairness, robustness, presentation) as the user asked. The game already had 22 rooms. Six MEDIUM findings and two LOW items were fixed and verified by a separate verification agent re-running the reviewers' own probes and one clean-worktree run, then by the browser check, without a second review round.
independentProbes: On the final files the fairness reviewer's marker-following bot (public getState only; doors, echo and prompt seen late) cleared all 22 rooms in 3 of 3 seeds at 0.25 s and 0.35 s, including room 14 with the echo-ring workaround disabled. Mastery pressure shows as slack rather than failures: recording-cap slack fell from about 7.3 s in combination rooms to about 1.45 s in mastery, door windows to 1.0-1.5 s, and mastery needs about 2.1 recordings per room against 1.6; the owner's slow human model (0.4-0.6 s) clears every room at least 28 of 30 times. Blind play cleared no rooms, final states matched across 30, 60 and 120 Hz, hostile dt and pointer values produced no throws or non-finite state, each run ended exactly once and froze, every broken progress store was safe, presses during the room-cleared pause now take effect, a soft-lock sweep left no unrecovered state, and EN and ZH text fits with no untranslated strings.

findings.observation: Robustness finding: createGame and clearRoom called env.progress without try/catch, so a throwing store crashed the game at start or at a room clear. All progress calls are now guarded as in Shield Sentinel.
Robustness finding: Space, X and Z pressed during the 0.8 s 'Room cleared!' pause were dropped. They are now buffered and applied when the pause ends.

Fairness finding: in room 14 a parked echo's 16 px body overlapped a neighbouring tile that the walk marker treated as free, leaving a player pushing into it with no hint. A parked echo now settles into the middle of its tile, so its footprint matches the path logic.

Fairness finding: mastery rooms were only slightly longer and had the most recording slack. Rooms 15-22 now use per-room recording caps of 3-8 s instead of 12 s, and timed and pair doors sized to the walk plus 1 s; rooms 1-14 and their full guidance are unchanged.

Presentation findings: moving and idle timeline segments, and locked and open menu rooms, differed only by colour. Idle segments are now a thin line against full-height moving blocks, and locked rooms show a padlock with a legend in EN and ZH.
The echo playhead now carries an arrow while replaying, and the description explains that Z restarts the room until a second room is unlocked.

openNotes: The walk marker still guides every room step by step, so mastery difficulty comes from tight recording caps and door windows rather than from finding the route.
Because the buffered post-clear press now starts a recording, a player who presses Space again at once stops that recording as too short.
The source is a single file of about 1,330 lines, over the repository's 800-line soft ceiling.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start and the language toggle, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: English: Start opened room 1 of 22 (First Echo) with the tip '[Space] An echo can stand on a plate for you', the plate, door A and the exit.

Space started a recording ('Recording: walk, then press Space'), a short walk and Space saved it ('Recording saved (1.3 s)'), and the timeline showed the moving stretch as a block and the idle stretch as a thin line; with the echo off the plate the prompt read 'Missed the plate: press Z to clear it'.
Chinese 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): room 1 in Chinese with touch buttons 左, 上, 下, 右, 录制/停止, 回放 and 重置 and the 12 s recording label in Chinese.
Not covered in the browser: a room clear, the mastery rooms and the padlocked menu; the reviewers' probes, the verification run and the quality tests cover them.
